title: Effectively Sanitizing Embedded Operating Systems
problem: Embedded operating systems lack effective testing with sanitizers, resulting in missed detection of subtle bugs that don't manifest as visible exceptions or errors. These latent bugs pose risks in security-critical deployments where embedded OSes are essential.
motivation: Embedded operating systems are widely deployed in security-critical applications where undetected bugs can have serious consequences.
method: The work applies sanitizers—dynamic analysis tools that instrument code to expose latent bugs—to embedded operating systems. Sanitizers detect memory safety, undefined behavior, and other issues that escape normal error handling during testing.
key_novelty: Systematic application of sanitizer technology to embedded operating systems to uncover previously undetected bugs in security-critical environments.
contributions: Demonstrates efficacy of sanitizers for embedded OS bug detection
Identifies previously hidden bugs through sanitizer instrumentation
Provides methodology for applying sanitizers to resource-constrained embedded environments
Shows critical value of sanitizer-based testing for security applications
limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in abstract; implementation details and overhead analysis unclear.
